Shared renderings: the Mesopotamian creation corpus

Binding for all projects in this folder (corpus.md). Echo tags follow guidelines §6.4: [cognate], [equivalent], [divergence], [absent].

0. Inheritance from the flood corpus

The flood corpus's shared renderings (../סיפורי-המבול-המסופוטמיים/renderings.md) are binding here as the default. Everything listed there (proper names, speech formulas, key terms, the false friends) applies unchanged unless this file overrides it. The items most often needed in the creation texts are copied below for convenience; the flood file is the authority for everything else.

Akkadian Hebrew From the flood corpus
Ea / Enki אֵאָה / אֶנְקִי same god; keep the name the text uses
Ellil / Enlil; Anu; Igigū; Anunnakkū אֶנְלִיל; אָנוּ; אִיגִיגִי; אֲנוּנָּכִּי
Nudimmud נוּדִימּוּד (= Ea)
Šamaš (the god) / šamšu (the sun) שַׁמַשׁ / שֶׁמֶשׁ
Apsû (הָ)אַפְּסוּ Not תְּהוֹם (false echo). See §1 for the person/place distinction in Enūma eliš.
Purattu / Idiqlat פְּרָת / חִדֶּקֶל [cognate] (בראשית ב:יד)
X pâšu īpuš(am)-ma iqabbi / izakkar(a) ana Y X פָּתַח אֶת פִּיו וְאָמַר, אֶל Y דִּבֵּר SB one-line formula. Over two lines: X פָּתַח אֶת פִּיו וְאָמַר, / דִּבֵּר אֶל Y:
ana šâšū-ma izakkar(a) דִּבֵּר אֵלָיו
qabû / zakāru (speech) אָמַר / דִּבֵּר
ilu, ilū, iltu; ilū rabûtu אֵל, אֵלִים, אֵלָה; הָאֵלִים הַגְּדוֹלִים Never אֱלֹהִים.
puḫru (puḫur ilī) אֲסֵפָה (אֲסֵפַת הָאֵלִים) Not עֵדָה.
šīmtu; šīmta šâmu גּוֹרָל; גָּזַר גּוֹרָל
banû בָּנָה [cognate]. Also of creating gods and man (cf. ב:כב). Not בָּרָא / יָצַר.
eṣēru, uṣurtu צָר, צוּרָה [cognate of יצר]
balālu בָּלַל [cognate]
lullû / awīlu (amēlu) / awīlūtu (amēlūtu) / nišū קַדְמוֹן / אָדָם / הָאֱנוֹשׁוּת / הָאֲנָשִׁים אָדָם/אֲדָמָה wordplay is Hebrew only.
dullu; šupšikku עָמָל; סַל The gods' toil laid on man.
damu; šīru; ṭiṭṭu דָּם; בָּשָׂר; טִיט
ṭēmu by sense (טַעַם / דַּעַת / עֵצָה / מַצָּב), with a note
šamû; erṣetu; mātu שָׁמַיִם; אֶרֶץ; אֶרֶץ [cognate] / [cognate] / [equivalent]
tâmtu / tiāmtu (the common noun "sea") יָם Cognate of תְּהוֹם: in the apparatus only. For the goddess, see §1.
nagbu מַעֲמַקִּים Not תְּהוֹם / מַעְיָנוֹת.
šāru; meḫû; ūmu (storm) רוּחַ; סוּפָה; סְעָרָה
ūmu; mūšu יוֹם; לַיְלָה
abūbu מַבּוּל [equivalent]; in Enūma eliš it is Marduk's weapon (IV 49, 75): note it.

1. Proper names (creation corpus)

Vocalize at the first occurrence in each text; afterwards plain spelling.

Akkadian (eBL) Hebrew Notes
Tiāmtu / Tiāmat (the goddess) תִּיאָמַת The name is the word tiāmtu "sea". First-occurrence note: cognate of תְהוֹם (בראשית א:ב) [cognate], not a loan (the Hebrew has no feminine -at and keeps the guttural); Hebrew תְּהוֹם is used without the article, almost as a name. The text never renders her תְּהוֹם. When the eBL lemma is the common noun tâmtu "sea", use יָם.
Apsû אַפְּסוּ (the god, Enūma eliš I 3–74); הָאַפְּסוּ (the place, from I 71 on) The god Apsû is killed and Ea builds his dwelling "upon Apsû" and names it Apsû (I 71–77). Without the article while he is a person, with it when he is the place. Note the shift at I 71/76. Not תְּהוֹם.
Mummu (Apsû's vizier); mummu (epithet of Tiāmat, I 4) מוּמּוּ; מוּמּוּ־תִּיאָמַת mummu means something like "creator, matrix, form" (CAD: "creative skill"?). In I 4 keep it as part of the name, with the meaning in a note.
Laḫmu and Laḫamu לַחְמוּ וְלַחָמוּ The first-born pair. The same word laḫmu "hairy one" is the name of a monster in Tiāmat's army (I 141 etc.) and of Ea's attendants (flood corpus: שְׂעִירִים). See the project renderings.
Anšar and Kišar אַנְשַׁר וְקִישַׁר "Whole of heaven" and "whole of earth" (Sumerian an.šár, ki.šár): note it at first occurrence.
Anu (Ānu) אָנוּ
Nudimmud / Ea נוּדִימּוּד / אֵאָה
Damkina דַּמְכִּינָה Ea's wife, Marduk's mother.
Marduk מַרְדּוּךְ First occurrence: note the biblical מְרֹדָךְ (ירמיהו נ:ב) and the epithet בֵּל (ישעיהו מו:א). The text form stays מַרְדּוּךְ.
Bēl (as Marduk's name) / bēlu (the common noun "lord") בֵּל / הָאָדוֹן בֵּל is the biblical form of the same word (ישעיהו מו:א; ירמיהו נ:ב; נא:מד) [cognate]. Use בֵּל only where the edition reads the name; elsewhere הָאָדוֹן.
Qingu קִינְגּוּ Tiāmat's second husband, from whose blood man is made.
Kakka (eBL; older "Gaga") גַּגָּא eBL normalizes Kakka; Hebrew קַקָּה would read as a nursery word, so we use the older reading גַּגָּא with a note. (Open decision for the user.)
Ḫubur חֻבּוּר "Mother Ḫubur" = Tiāmat (I 133); also the river of the netherworld.
Nannaru (the moon god; "luminary") נַנָּרוּ Not מָאוֹר / יָרֵחַ. The name means "luminary": note it at every Gen 1:14–16 comparison [equivalent ↔ הַמָּאוֹר הַקָּטֹן, א:טז].
Sîn סִין
Enlil, Anu, Ea as a triad אָנוּ, אֶנְלִיל וְאֵאָה
Igigū / Anunnakkū אִיגִיגִי / אֲנוּנָּכִּי
Lugaldimmerankia (Marduk's name, VI 28 etc.) and the other fifty names transliterated, hyphenated by its Sumerian elements, e.g. לוּגַל־דִּימֶר־אַנְקִיָּה; the text's own explanation is translated The names are explained by learned etymology; the apparatus gives the Sumerian.
Esagil; Ešarra; Ešgalla; Ekur; Ubšukkinnaku אֵסַגִּיל; אֵשַׁרָּה; אֵשְׁגַלָּה; אֵכּוּר; אוּבְּשׁוּכִּינַּכּוּ Temple names are transliterated; their meaning goes in a note ("house whose head is raised", "house of totality" …).
Babylon (Bābili, "gate of the gods") בָּבֶל Biblical form (guidelines §6.4). Note the folk etymology bāb ilī and Gen 11:9.
Nēberu (Marduk's star) נֵבֶרוּ "Crossing point"; root ebēru ~ עבר [cognate].

2. Formulas specific to Enūma eliš

Set before drafting; every recurrence must match (guidelines §6.1). The long repeated passages (Tiāmat's army, Marduk's conditions) are fixed in the project renderings, 1-אנומה-אליש/renderings.md.

Akkadian Hebrew Notes
X pâšu īpuš-ma iqabbi / ana Y amāta izakkar X פָּתַח אֶת פִּיו וְאָמַר, / אֶל Y דָּבָר דִּבֵּר When amāta is present, render it (דָּבָר).
amāta izakkar / amāta iqabbi דָּבָר דִּבֵּר / דָּבָר אָמַר
išmē-ma X amāta šuāti שָׁמַע X אֶת הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה
ītamû / atmû שָׂח atmû "to speak (to)" ≠ zakāru.
ṣīt pî מוֹצָא פִּי [cognate: aṣû = יצא] (דברים ח:ג; במדבר ל:יג).
epšu pî / epēš pî מַעֲשֵׂה פִּי
šīmta šâmu גָּזַר גּוֹרָל
ṭuppi šīmāti לוּחַ הַגּוֹרָלוֹת
ḫamšā šumī חֲמִשִּׁים שֵׁמוֹת
mutīr gimilli הַמֵּשִׁיב גְּמוּל "avenger" (gimillu ~ גְּמוּל [cognate]).
ina ubšukkinnakki בְּאוּבְּשׁוּכִּינַּכּוּ The assembly hall.
ilū abbūšu הָאֵלִים, אֲבוֹתָיו

3. Key terms that touch Genesis 1–3

These are the decisions that matter most for the comparison. Each has its tag; in every occurrence the apparatus names the Akkadian word behind the Hebrew.

Akkadian (eBL lemma) Hebrew Tag Reason / rejected alternatives
nabû (G "to name, call"; N "to be named") קָרָא (שֵׁם / בְּשֵׁם); N: נִקְרָא [equivalent] ↔ וַיִּקְרָא (א:ה, ח, י) The main naming verb (I 1; the fifty names). Not cognate of קרא (nabû ~ נָבִיא).
šuma zakāru (G/D "to name, to pronounce a name") הִזְכִּיר שֵׁם [cognate] (zakāru = זכר; שמות כ:כ אַזְכִּיר אֶת שְׁמִי) Kept apart from nabû so the reader sees which verb stands where (I 2, 8, 10).
šumu שֵׁם [cognate]
zikru "name, fame" / "utterance, command" (st. constr. siqar) זֵכֶר / מַאֲמָר [cognate] (זֵכֶר "name", שמות ג:טו; הושע יב:ו) Override of the flood corpus's שֵׁם for zikru, so that šumu and zikru stay apart in the fifty names.
kataduggû; qibītu אִמְרָה; אֲמִירָה
kânu G "to be firm"; D kunnu "to establish" נָכוֹן, יִכּוֹן; כּוֹנֵן [cognate] ↔ וַיְהִי כֵן (א:ז ועוד; כֵּן is from the same root) IV 22 qibi liktūnā "command, and let them be firm" ↔ the creation by word.
epēšu עָשָׂה [equivalent] ↔ וַיַּעַשׂ (א:ז, טז, כה)
bašû Š (šubšû) "to bring into being" הֵבִיא לִכְלַל הֲוָיָה [equivalent] ↔ וַיִּבְרָא (א:כא) Used of Tiāmat creating the eleven monsters (I 146). Not בָּרָא (false echo); הִמְצִיא is too modern.
bašāmu "to design, form" תִּכֵּן Isa 40:12 וְשָׁמַיִם בַּזֶּרֶת תִּכֵּן. Not יָצַר (kept for eṣēru) and not עִצֵּב (kept for patāqu).
patāqu "to shape, mould (bricks, metal)" עִצֵּב (מְעַצֶּבֶת) I 133 Ḫubur "who shapes everything"; V 65 iptiq šamê u erṣeti; VI 58 the bricks of Babylon. In this sense עִצֵּב has nothing to do with עֶצֶב (sorrow, ג:טז): vocalize when ambiguous.
nabnītu "creature, form, offspring" מִבְנֶה, pl. מִבְנִים (form, stature, creature – also the eleven monsters, IV 115, V 73); יְלוּד (offspring, when the sense is birth) From banû: the Hebrew keeps the root בנה. Never בְּרִיָּה / יְצוּר / תּוֹלָדָה (each would pre-empt a Genesis word).
binûtu "creation, build" מִבְנֶה
tamšīlu "likeness, replica" תַּבְנִית [equivalent] ↔ בִּדְמוּתוֹ כְּצַלְמוֹ (ה:ג); בִּדְמוּת אֱלֹהִים (ה:א) I 16: Anu begot Nudimmud, his likeness ↔ Gen 5:3. Not דְּמוּת (would pre-empt). The root is mšl (Heb. מָשַׁל "to liken").
mašālu D "to make equal, liken" הִמְשִׁיל (לְ־) [cognate] (ישעיהו מו:ה וְתַמְשִׁלוּנִי וְנִדְמֶה) I 15, 138.
ṣalmu צֶלֶם [cognate] ↔ בְּצַלְמֵנוּ (א:כו–כז) V 75: the images of the eleven monsters set at the Apsû gate as a "sign".
ittu אוֹת [cognate] ↔ לְאֹתֹת (א:יד); אוֹת הַבְּרִית (ט:יב–יג)
ḫepû "to split, break" בִּקַּע [equivalent] IV 101, 137. Cf. תהלים עד:יג–טו; ז:יא נִבְקְעוּ.
parāsu "to separate, cut off; decide"; purussû הִפְרִיד; גָּזַר; גְּזֵרָה [equivalent] ↔ וַיַּבְדֵּל (א:ד, ז) Not הִבְדִּיל, which would pre-empt the comparison; Akkadian has no cognate of בדל.
zâzu "to divide, apportion" (D uzaʾʾiz) חִלֵּק [equivalent] ↔ בְּהַנְחֵל עֶלְיוֹן גּוֹיִם (דברים לב:ח) VI 39–46: Marduk divides the Anunnakkū between heaven and earth.
mišlu "half" מַחֲצִית IV 138, V 62: half of Tiāmat.
šamû / šamāmū שָׁמַיִם [cognate] šamāmū is poetic; the apparatus says which.
ṣullulu "to roof (over)" (IV 138 šamāmī uṣṣallil; V 62) קֵרָה (בְּקוֹרוֹת) [divergence] ↔ רָקִיעַ (א:ו–ח); [equivalent] ↔ הַמְקָרֶה בַמַּיִם עֲלִיּוֹתָיו (תהלים קד:ג) From the flood corpus (ṣullulu = קֵרָה). Akkadian has no raqīʿu: Marduk's sky is half of Tiāmat set up as a roof, with a skin stretched and guards posted so that her waters cannot escape. רָקִיעַ is never used in the translation.
šadādu "to draw, stretch" (+ mašku "skin, hide") מָתַח (אֶת הָעוֹר) [equivalent] ↔ נוֹטֶה שָׁמַיִם כַּיְרִיעָה (תהלים קד:ב); רֹקַע הָאָרֶץ (ישעיהו מב:ה) IV 139. The eBL reading is maška "skin"; the older reading parka "bar, bolt" is noted.
maṣṣaru; maṣṣartu נוֹצֵר (pl. נוֹצְרִים); מִשְׁמֶרֶת [cognate] (naṣāru = נצר; ירמיהו ד:טז נֹצְרִים) IV 139; VI 42.
elâti; išid šamê הַמְּרוֹמִים; יְסוֹד הַשָּׁמַיִם (= the horizon)
ammatu (poetic "firm ground, earth") קַרְקַע I 2. Not הַיַּבָּשָׁה (א:ט) and not אֲדָמָה.
kakkabu; lumāšu "constellation" כּוֹכָב [cognate]; מַזָּל, pl. מַזָּלוֹת Note that Hebrew לַמַּזָּלוֹת (מלכים ב כג:ה) comes from Akk. manzaltu "station", not from lumāšu. IV 19–26, V 2.
manzāzu (of a star or god) מְקוֹם עֲמִידָה Flood corpus (not מָנוֹחַ). Note the link manzaltu / מַזָּל.
uddû (D of idû) "to mark, assign, make known" סִמֵּן [equivalent] ↔ וְהָיוּ לְאֹתֹת וּלְמוֹעֲדִים וּלְיָמִים וְשָׁנִים (א:יד) V 3, 13. Root idû = ידע [cognate], noted. Not יִעֵד (would pre-empt מוֹעֲדִים).
šattu שָׁנָה [cognate]
agû (crown; the lunar disk); qarnu כֶּתֶר; קֶרֶן [cognate] (qarnu)
nūru; namāru / nawāru אוֹר; הֵאִיר [equivalent]
šuʾpû / šūpû "to make appear, make shine" הוֹפִיעַ V 12 the moon; IV 26.
imtu; bašmu; ušumgallu; mušmaḫḫu; mušḫuššu … see the project renderings (the eleven monsters) [equivalent] ↔ הַתַּנִּינִם הַגְּדֹלִים (א:כא) Never תַּנִּין for any of them. The comparison with Gen 1:21 is made in the apparatus, not by the Hebrew word.
dalāḫu "to stir up, roil (water); disturb" דָּלַח (pi. דִּלַּח); stative: דָּלוּחַ [cognate] ↔ וַתִּדְלַח מַיִם בְּרַגְלֶיךָ, said of the תַּנִּים in the seas (יחזקאל לב:ב) I 108–109; II 49 etc.
ḫiāqu "to mingle" נִמְזַג I 5 (the waters). Not בָּלַל (kept for balālu).
nâḫu G; D nuḫḫu; nēḫtu; tanēḫtu נָח; הֵנִיחַ (also "to calm" – cf. וַהֲנִחוֹתִי חֲמָתִי, יחזקאל ה:יג); מְנוּחָה; מְנוּחָה [cognate] ↔ וַיָּנַח בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי (שמות כ:י) Gen 2:2–3 has וַיִּשְׁבֹּת: [equivalent].
pašāḫu G "to rest, be relieved"; Š šupšuḫu; tapšuḫtu נִרְגַּע; הִרְגִּיעַ; מַרְגּוֹעַ [equivalent] ↔ וַיִּשְׁבֹּת (ב:ב–ג); וַיִּנָּפַשׁ (שמות לא:יז) Cf. ישעיהו לד:יד הִרְגִּיעָה … וּמָצְאָה לָהּ מָנוֹחַ. Akkadian has no verb šabātu "to rest".
ṣalālu; sakāpu; šittu יָשֵׁן (Š: יִשֵּׁן); שָׁכַב; שֵׁנָה I 38 etc. Narrowed after Tablet I.
šasû "to cry out, call" צָעַק So that קָרָא stays exclusive for nabû (Tablet I).
nubattu מָלוֹן "Night's lodging, resting place" (V 126; VI 52).
šubtu; šubat nēḫti מוֹשָׁב; מוֹשַׁב מְנוּחָה
rēšu + ullû הֵרִים אֶת רֹאשׁוֹ [cognate] (rēšu = ראש) ↔ וְרֹאשׁוֹ בַשָּׁמַיִם (יא:ד) VI 62 Esagil.
labānu "to make bricks"; libittu לָבַן (לְבֵנִים); לְבֵנָה [cognate] ↔ נִלְבְּנָה לְבֵנִים (יא:ג) VI 60.
ziqqurratu זִקּוּרַת [divergence] ↔ מִגְדָּל (יא:ד)
qaštu קֶשֶׁת [cognate] ↔ אֶת קַשְׁתִּי נָתַתִּי בֶּעָנָן (ט:יג) IV 35ff; VI 82–91.
erpetu; imbaru עָנָן; עֲרָפֶל [equivalent] Note the proposed cognacy erpetu ~ עֲרָפֶל.
eṣemtu עֶצֶם [cognate] ↔ עֶצֶם מֵעֲצָמַי (ב:כג) VI 5.
ṣēlu "rib, side" צֵלָע [cognate] ↔ מִצַּלְעֹתָיו (ב:כא) V 9 "on both sides".
gerû "to be hostile"; tuqumtu הִתְגָּרָה; תִּגְרָה [cognate?] (משלי טו:יח יְגָרֶה מָדוֹן)
tāḫāzu; qablu; tamḫāru; anantu; ṣūlātu מִלְחָמָה; קְרָב; מַעֲרָכָה; מָדוֹן; מְהוּמוֹת Five battle words, five Hebrew words.
kakku נֶשֶׁק
melammu; pulḫātu (pl. of puluḫtu) זֹהַר; אֵימוֹת
ummānu (army) חַיִל Not צָבָא (would pre-empt וְכָל צְבָאָם, ב:א).
ukkinnu (assembly) מוֹעֵצָה Kept apart from puḫru = אֲסֵפָה.
bukru צֶאֱצָא [cognate of בְּכוֹר, different meaning] māru = בֵּן.
māḫāzu מָחוֹז [cognate] (תהלים קז:ל מְחוֹז חֶפְצָם) "Cult city": note at first occurrence.
parakku; kussû; ekallu דּוּכָן; כִּסֵּא; הֵיכָל [cognate] (kussû, ekallu)
parṣu פֻּלְחָן (pl. פֻּלְחָנִים) "Cultic office, rite".
šarru; šarrūtu; bēlūtu; malikūtu; anūtu מֶלֶךְ; מַלְכוּת; אֲדָנוּת; שִׁלְטוֹן; שְׂרָרַת אָנוּ
ṣīt pî; epšu pî מוֹצָא פִּי; מַעֲשֵׂה פִּי (§2)

4. False friends met in this corpus

  • tiāmtu ↔ תְּהוֹם: a real cognate, but the Hebrew word is not a name of a goddess in Genesis; never render the goddess as תְּהוֹם.
  • apsû ↔ אֶפֶס ("end"): the sound is close, the words are unrelated (Sumerian abzu). Note it once.
  • nabû "to name" ↔ נָבָא: cognate, but not the Hebrew sense "prophesy".
  • šapattu ↔ שַׁבָּת: the 15th day of the month, not a day of rest.
  • bukru ↔ בְּכוֹר: in jB "son, offspring", not specifically the firstborn.
  • pašāḫu "to rest" has nothing to do with פֶּסַח.

5. Added from project 2 (the creation and Eden companions), 2026-10-17

Merged by the corpus coordinator from the seven texts' proposals (2-טקסטי-בריאה-ועדן/project.md); the project's own renderings.md has the full tables. These rows bind every later project of the corpus (and are the default for Sumerian texts elsewhere).

Sum. ĝal₂: placing an object = נָתַן; intransitive = קַיָּם; bringing into existence = הֵבִיא לִכְלַל הֲוָיָה (= šubšû).

5.3 Traps of unvocalized Hebrew (string collisions with reserved words)

בראותו, בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה, בָּרֹאשׁ (ב־ר־א: use כִּרְאוֹתוֹ, תְּחִלָּה, רִאשׁוֹן); לשבת "to sit" (use לֵישֵׁב); שבתומל (use אשר בתומל); שדמות (contains דמות); עצבה vs עיצבה (write plene); נעשה = נַעֲשָׂה / נַעֲשֶׂה (vocalize); בשמים "spices" / "in heaven", חלבו "his milk" / "his fat", שכנו "dwelt" / Šakkan (vocalize); עֵין הַחַיִּים sounds like עֵץ הַחַיִּים (keep the idiom, note the Hebrew-only assonance).

5.4 Open between projects 1 and 2

  • ṭeḫû: Enūma eliš קָרַב; project 2 נִגַּשׁ (Adapa has both qerēbu and ṭeḫû). Proposal: נִגַּשׁ corpus-wide, Enūma eliš's âru then needs another verb. Left for the user.
  • šipru: still פֹּעַל (project 1 open decision 4); project 2 has no occurrence.

6. Fixed before projects 3–4 (Bird and Fish; Enki and the World Order), 2026-10-19

Set by the corpus coordinator before drafting. Binding for both projects; the translators add rows to their project's renderings.md and propose changes in project.md. Everything in §0–§5 (and project 2's renderings.md §1–§2 and its Text 2–5 rows for Sumerian) applies; this section adds and narrows. Checked by sumerian_tools.py verify (reserved strings and name traps).

6.1 The creatures of the fifth day (↔ בראשית א:כ–כג)

Sumerian Hebrew Tag Notes
mušen (bird; also the determinative of flying creatures) צִפּוֹר, pl. צִפֳּרִים; personified Bird: צִפּוֹר (no article, feminine) [equivalent] ↔ וְעוֹף יְעוֹפֵף (א:כ); כֹּל צִפּוֹר כָּל כָּנָף (ז:יד) Not עוֹף. In the commentary's dictionary עוֹף names a creature by its motion ("what flies"), and צִפּוֹר is the kind (בראשית ז:יד). Sumerian mušen is the kind-word; it is the verb dal "to fly" that names the motion. Keeping them apart lets the reader see which the Sumerian uses where. (Project 2 has עוֹף for mušen in E&Nḫ 18 and Hoe 83, and צִפּוֹר for buru₅ in G&S 173: open decision 1 of project 3.)
dal "to fly" (Akk. naprušu) עָף; iterative/reduplicated: עוֹפֵף [equivalent] ↔ יְעוֹפֵף (א:כ) The only licensed עוף string (checked by script).
pa / pa-pa "wing(s)"; a₂ (of a bird) "wing, arm" כָּנָף; a₂: כָּנָף with a note "lit. arm" [equivalent] ↔ כָּל עוֹף כָּנָף (א:כא)
ku₆ (fish) דָּג, pl. דָּגִים; personified Fish: דָּג (no article, masculine) [equivalent] ↔ שֶׁרֶץ נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה (א:כ); בִדְגַת הַיָּם (א:כו) Fish species (suḫur, eštub, suḫurmaš …) are transliterated with a note (דַּג־הַסּוּחוּר).

6.2 Order, allotment and the me

Sumerian Hebrew Tag Notes
me הַ־מֶה (always vocalized: unvocalized המה = "they", מה = "what"); plural agreement: הַ־מֶה הַגְּדוֹלִים, הַ־מֶה הַטְּהוֹרִים As project 2 (G&S 56). The note explains the me (the god-given powers, offices and arts that make a civilization run) at the first occurrence of each text; the reader's introduction explains it too. The flood corpus renders me maḫ הַכֹּחוֹת הַנִּשְׂגָּבִים (project 3 there): a cross-corpus split, open decision 2 of project 4.
ĝiš-ḫur "design, plan, drawing" (Akk. uṣurtu) צוּרָה, pl. צוּרוֹת [equivalent] (Akk. uṣurtu is the cognate of יצר) The Sumerian takes the Hebrew of its Akkadian equivalent (§0, eṣēru, uṣurtu).
nam tar / nam … tar; nam dug₃ גָּזַר גּוֹרָל; גּוֹרָל טוֹב [divergence] ↔ וַיְבָרֶךְ אֹתָם אֱלֹהִים (א:כב) Enki "decrees the fate" of a land or a creature where Genesis "blesses": never בֵּרַךְ for nam tar. בֵּרַךְ only for a verb "to bless/pray" (šud₃; ka-aš bar is a decision: הִכְרִיעַ).
ugula "overseer"; the EWO appointment formula is in fact {d}en-ki-ke₄ zag-ba nam-mi-in-gub "Enki set (him) standing at its side" = אֶנְקִי לְצִדּוֹ הֶעֱמִיד (corrected after the first EWO run: there is no ugula … ĝar); gu₂-gal "canal inspector"; šu … si / šu-ni-še₃ ĝar "entrust" פָּקִיד; מְפַקֵּחַ (with the object: מְפַקֵּחַ הַתְּעָלוֹת); שָׂם בְּיָדוֹ [equivalent] ↔ וְיַפְקֵד פְּקִדִים עַל הָאָרֶץ (מא:לד); בְּהַנְחֵל עֶלְיוֹן גּוֹיִם (דברים לב:ח) ĝar = שָׂם (§5.2, reserved).
ki-sur-ra "border"; ki-sur-ra ĝar; ki-tuš "dwelling"; ki-gub "standing place" גְּבוּל; שָׂם גְּבוּלוֹת (gub "set up" = הֶעֱמִיד); מוֹשָׁב; מְקוֹם עֲמִידָה [equivalent] ↔ יַצֵּב גְּבֻלֹת עַמִּים (דברים לב:ח) ki-gub = manzāzu (§3).
ud; iti; mu (year); šid "count"; iti … e₂-ba ku₄ "make the months enter their houses" יוֹם; יֶרַח; שָׁנָה; מָנָה; הַיְּרָחִים אֶל בָּתֵּיהֶם הֵבִיא (literal) [equivalent] ↔ וְהָיוּ לְאֹתֹת וּלְמוֹעֲדִים וּלְיָמִים וְשָׁנִים (א:יד) iti = Akk. warḫu = יֶרַח (§0). mu "year" / mu "name": the apparatus says which.
šeĝ₃ (verb) / im-šeĝ₃ (noun) הִמְטִיר / מָטָר [equivalent] ↔ כִּי לֹא הִמְטִיר יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים עַל הָאָרֶץ (ב:ה)
numun "seed"; zid "true, good, right" זֶרַע; אֱמֶת (זֶרַע אֱמֶת, ירמיהו ב:כא; טְלֵה אֱמֶת) [equivalent] zid is never טוֹב (reserved for dug₃) and never כֵּן (reserved for kânu).
a₂ aĝ₂ "instruct, command"; inim "word"; inim dug₄ צִוָּה; דָּבָר; אָמַר דָּבָר [equivalent] ↔ וַיְצַו יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים (ב:טז)

6.4 Names (vocalized at the first occurrence of each text; Utu, Uttu, Inana and Magan at every occurrence, checked by script for the first three)

Enki אֶנְקִי; Nudimmud נוּדִימּוּד; An אַן; Enlil אֶנְלִיל; the Anuna הָאֲנוּנָּה; Ninḫursaĝa נִין־חֻרְסַגָּה; Nintur נִינְתּוּר; Aruru אֲרוּרוּ (not אָרוּר); Inana אִינַנָּה (always vocalized: איננה = "is not"); Utu אוּתוּ; Uttu אוּטּוּ; Šakkan שַׁכַּן; Dumuzid דּוּמוּזִי; Ezina (Grain) דָּגָן; Nanše נַנְשֶׁה; Iškur אִישְׁכּוּר; Nisaba נִיסַבָּה; Šulgi שׁוּלְגִּי; Eridug אֶרִידוּ; Nibru נִיפּוּר; Ekur אֵכּוּר; Urim אוּר (the biblical form, note אוּר כַּשְׂדִּים, בראשית יא:כח); Sumer שׁוּמֶר; Dilmun דִּלְמוּן; Magan מָגָן; Meluḫḫa מֶלוּחָה; Elam עֵילָם; Marḫaši מַרְחַשִׁי; Martu מַרְטוּ (the Amorites; note הָאֱמֹרִי, בראשית י:טז, without assimilating); Tigris / Euphrates חִדֶּקֶל / פְּרָת. New EWO names (Enbilulu, Enkimdu, Kulla, Mušdama, Ninsikila, Ninisina, Ninmug, Sirsir, Niĝir-sig, Kulaba, E-engura …) are set by the first EWO translator.

שֶׁרֶץ, רֶמֶשׂ, תַּנִּין, נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה, לְמִינֵהוּ, פְּרוּ וּרְבוּ, בָּרָא (also inside בראותו, בראשונה), יָצַר, עֵדֶן, רָקִיעַ, תְּהוֹם, הִבְדִּיל, טֶרֶם, עוֹלָם, אֲדָמָה, מְלָאכָה, צֶלֶם, דְּמוּת; עוף only for dal; כָּנָף only for pa / a₂; טוֹב only for dug₃; בֵּרַךְ only for šud₃ (or בֶּרֶךְ "knee", dub₃); עבד only for kiĝ₂.

7. Merged from project 3 (Bird and Fish), 2026-10-19

From 3-הציפור-והדג/project.md ("Proposals") and its renderings.md (full rows with lines). Binding for project 4 and later Sumerian texts of the corpus.

  • Marsh and water: umaḫ = גֶּבֶא (ישעיהו ל:יד); sug = אֲגַם (apart from ambar = בִּצָּה); sur₃ = חָרִיץ (apart from pa₅ = תְּעָלָה); agargara = דְּגִיגִים; pu₂-kiri₆ = פַּרְדֵּס, nu-kiri₆ = גַּנָּן.
  • Herding: unud = בּוֹקֵר (cf. בוֹקֵר אָנֹכִי, עמוס ז:יד); tur₃ = רֶפֶת; amaš = דִּיר (§5.2).
  • Sound: za-pa-aĝ₂ = שָׁאוֹן; mu₇ = הָמָה / הֶמְיָה; akkil = רִנָּה; mur ša₄ = נָהַם.
  • Verbs: sig₁₀ = שָׁת (always vocalized; עֵצָה שָׁת for sa₂ sig₁₀); gir₅ = חָמַק; DU.DU / du-du = הִתְהַלֵּךְ; ad gi₄ = נִמְלַךְ (= Akk. malāku); en₃ tar = דָּרַשׁ; kiĝ₂ (verb) = בִּקֵּשׁ (the noun stays עֲבוֹדָה); gul = הָרַס; bal = הָפַךְ; la₂ = מָתַח, of the neck הִטָּה; keše₂ = קָשַׁר; us₂ = דָּבַק; saĝ-e-eš rig₇ = הֶעֱנִיק בְּמַתָּנָה; šu ĝar gi₄ = הֵשִׁיב גְּמוּל. (sig₉ is הֵטִיל in Enki and Ninmaḫ, דְּמָמָה "quiet" in B&F 103, 105: different words.)
  • Beings and things: gal₅-la₂ = שֵׁד־גַּלָּה; piriĝ = לָבִיא (ur-maḫ = אַרְיֵה); ḫu-ri₂-in = נֶשֶׁר; za-gin₃ = סַפִּיר; nidba = קָרְבָּן (apart from sa₂-dug₄ = מִנְחָה קְבוּעָה); ĝišbun = מִשְׁתֶּה; banšur = שֻׁלְחָן; e₂-gal = הֵיכָל [cognate: Sum. e₂-gal > Akk. ekallu > הֵיכָל].
  • Qualities: me-te = עֲדִי; ḫe₂-du₇ = תִּפְאֶרֶת; nam-maḫ = רוֹמְמוּת, maḫ = נִשְׂגָּב; gal-zu = בָּקִי; gur₄ = עָבֶה (pride); sag₉ = נָאֶה, noun נוֹי; ku₇ = מָתוֹק; zil₂ = נָעִים; gun₃ = סַסְגּוֹנִי; galam = נוֹכֵל (עָרוּם reserved for בראשית ג:א); a₂-ur₂ "limbs" = אֵבֶר.
  • Debate formulas (§6.3 confirmed): šag₄-še₃ nu-gid₂ = אֶל לִבּוֹ לֹא מָשַׁךְ; gu₂ ki-še₃ la₂ = הַטֵּה צַוָּארְךָ אַרְצָה; ni₂-zu ad li-bi₂-gi₄ = עִם עַצְמְךָ לֹא נִמְלַכְתָּ.

8. Merged from project 4 (Enki and the World Order), 2026-10-19

The full rows (with lines) are in 4-אנקי-וסדר-העולם/renderings.md and its project.md ("Proposals"); the most reusable:

  • The EWO formulas (replace the ugula guess of §6.2): {d}en-ki-ke₄ zag-ba nam-mi-in-gub = אֶנְקִי לְצִדּוֹ הֶעֱמִיד. (13×); e₂-kur-re e₂ {d}en-lil₂-la₂-ke₄ niĝ₂ ĝal₂-la nam-si = אֶת הָאֵכּוּר, בֵּית אֶנְלִיל, נְכָסִים מִלֵּא;; {d}en-ki-da {d}en-lil₂ mu-un-da-ḫul₂ nibru{ki} giri₁₇-zal-am₃ = עִם אֶנְקִי שָׂמַח אֶנְלִיל, נִיפּוּר – שְׂמֵחָה הִיא.; X gu₃ ba-an-de₂ = אֶל X פָּנָה (never קָרָא); a-na a-ra-an-la₂ a-na a-ra-ab-taḫ-e-de₃-en = מָה הִמְעַטְתִּי לָךְ? מָה אוֹסִיף לָךְ?; nam im-mi-ib-tar-re = אֶת גּוֹרָלָהּ גּוֹזֵר:; ud e₃ … ud šu₂ = מִצֵּאת הַיּוֹם עַד בּוֹא הַיּוֹם (G&S's formula with ud for {d}utu).
  • Verbs: si … sa₂ = יִשֵּׁר (= Akk. šūšuru); dub "heap" = עָרַם; du₇ = הִשְׁלִים / "gore" נָגַח; ri = נָשָׂא (לָקַח kept for leqû); šu ti = קִבֵּל; taḫ / lal = הוֹסִיף / הִמְעִיט; ĝiš₃ dug₄ = בָּעַל; a ri = הִזְרִיעַ; pad₃ by sense (בָּחַר, מָצָא, נָקַב); tum₂ = הוֹבִיל (de₆ = הֵבִיא); dib = עָבַר; mar = הִנִּיחַ (not ĝar).
  • Nouns: ĝarza₂ / mar-za = פֻּלְחָן (= parṣu, §3); in "zone" = תְּחוּם; bulug = יָתֵד; guru₇ = כְּרִי [cognate loan]; šeg₁₂ = לְבֵנָה (= libittu); ki-šar₂ = תֵּבֵל (never עוֹלָם); ma₂-laḫ₅ = מַלָּח and gu-za = כִּסֵּא [cognate loans]; ušumgal = דְּרָקוֹן־עֲנָק (confirmed; tagged ↔ א:כא, never תַּנִּין); la-ḫa-ma = הַלַּחַמָּה; buru₅ = צִפּוֹר; ensi₂ = מוֹשֵׁל; nu-banda₃ = מְמֻנֶּה; tibira = צוֹרֵף; šag₄-zu = מְיַלֶּדֶת; dub-sar = סוֹפֵר.
  • Names: Enbilulu, Enkimdu, Kulla, Mušdama, Ninsikila, Ninisina, Ninmug, Nisaba, Sirsir, Niĝir-sig: project 4 renderings (Nisaba must be harmonized with the Song of the Hoe: project 4 open decision 17). Urim אוּר and Sumer שׁוּמֶר are always vocalized (אור "light", שומר "guard").
  • String traps (§5.3): דברך (ברך), בראש (ברא), סוחורמש (רמש: write סוּחוּר־מַשׁ).
